title: The stationary diagonal squeeze problem reduces exactly to one variance parameter

profile_reduction.continuum_data: On Q=[-1,1]^3 write r=|x| and c_C=(1/2)int_Q r^(-1)dx. For a positive squeeze profile s define A[s]=(1/2)int_Q s/r dx and F[s]=(1/4)int_Q r(s+s^(-1)-2)dx.
profile_reduction.fixed_variance_minimizer: For every 0<A<c_C there is a unique kappa>0 with A=A(kappa):=(1/2)int_Q(r^2+kappa)^(-1/2)dx, and the unique minimizer of F at A[s]=A is s_kappa(x)=r/sqrt(r^2+kappa).
profile_reduction.proof: The free integrand is strictly convex in s and the variance constraint is linear. Its Euler equation is r(1-s^(-2))/4+mu/(2r)=0, hence s=r/sqrt(r^2+2mu). Strict convexity gives the global minimizer; monotone convergence makes A(kappa) strictly decrease from c_C to 0.
profile_reduction.reduced_derivative: If F_*(A)=F[s_(kappa(A))], the envelope theorem gives F_*'(A)=-kappa(A)/2.
profile_reduction.ratio_monotonicity: With D(kappa)=c_C-A(kappa), R(kappa)=kappa/D(kappa) is strictly increasing from 0 to infinity. Indeed D+kappa A' is the integral of the positive pointwise function [2(1-(1+t)^(-1/2))-t(1+t)^(-3/2)]/(4r), t=kappa/r^2.
profile_reduction.uniform_comparison: At any fixed 0<A<c_C the uniform profile s=A/c_C is admissible but is not s_kappa almost everywhere, so strict convexity makes its free coefficient strictly larger while the optimized interaction coefficient is unchanged.
profile_reduction.scope_guard: This is a continuum leading-coefficient theorem for translation-invariant diagonal Gaussian Q-space trials. It is not an unrestricted lower bound, a non-Gaussian classification, a bounded-error lattice expansion, a ground-state profile theorem or a source-owned Hamiltonian.
